title: Stability matrix and stochastic seed-locking for benchmark reproducibility
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our CI benchmark results for kernel selection and prefill/decode scheduling are noisy across runs due to stochastic workload sampling and non-deterministic seeds in mixbench. This produces flakey CI perf gates and weak signal for the attention-optimization changes we need to prioritize.

Goal: Introduce a stability matrix and deterministic seed-locking layer in the benchmark harness to reduce variance, provide drift-resistant baselines, and produce CI perf gates that meaningfully reflect regressions in kernel routing, attention optimizations, and prefill/decode scheduling. The work should preserve representative diversity in workload suites while enabling reproducible golden baseline comparisons.

Scope:
- Implement run-level seed-locking for mixbench workload sampler (prefill + decode phases).
- Add a stability matrix artifact: cross-product of model-variant x seq-length-profile x batch-shape x kernel-config to track per-cell median/95th quantile across N locked runs.
- Extend runner to emit per-run deterministic metadata (random_seed, node-kernel-map, hardware-abi-tag).
- Add CI perf gate logic that compares stability-matrix cells against regression thresholds and fails only when cell drift exceeds both relative and absolute thresholds for two successive runs.
- Preserve stochastic sampling by rotating locked seed-sets monthly to avoid overfitting to one fixed corpus.

Why different from existing work: Existing tasks focused on golden baselines and workload templating; this ticket focuses on reducing run-to-run noise at the harness level via seed-locking and a compact stability matrix that enables statistical gating rather than brittle single-number thresholds. It also ties metadata about kernel routing decisions to the benchmark outputs to make it possible to correlate regressions with kernel selection changes.
acceptance_criteria: Bench harness can run a locked-seed mixbench workload with --seed N and emit deterministic metadata headers
Stability matrix artifact generated after 3 locked runs with per-cell median and p95 values recorded in storage
CI perf gate script consumes the stability matrix and flags regressions only when both absolute and relative thresholds are exceeded in consecutive pipeline runs
Reduced CI flakiness: measured decrease in false-positive perf gate failures by >= 60% over 30 daily runs
Links to example Grafana dashboard panels for stability-matrix cells and a PR with unit/integration tests

comments: 2026-03-10 Aisha Patel: Kickoff — defined scope and trade-offs. We will not change sampling distributions immediately; first step is seed-lock to reduce variance. Referenced ENG-61234 for adaptive mixbench context.

2026-03-11 Marco Liang: Prototype seed-lock in local runner. Observed deterministic prefills but decode-phase randomness still present due to kernel scheduling non-determinism on multi-GPU runs — investigating adding node-kernel-map in metadata.

2026-03-11 Riley Johnson: Design note — we'll add a lightweight per-run header file (JSONL) with random_seed, affinity_map, kernel_selection_hash, and environment tags (cuda/cuDNN versions). This will allow posthoc grouping for noise analysis.

2026-03-12 Samir Gupta: Implemented stability matrix writer that collapses runs into cells keyed by (model, seq_profile, batch_shape, kernel_config). Stored as ndjson in s3://redwood-perf/stability-matrices/runtime-1.22/. Initial 3-run run shows cell p95 variance reduced by ~40% for short-seq models.

2026-03-12 Marco Liang: CI gate draft PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8621. Gate requires two consecutive CI runs where cell drift > abs_threshold AND > relative_threshold before failing. Seeking review from eng/perf and SRE.

2026-03-12 Aisha Patel: Note on trade-offs — locking seeds improves reproducibility but risks overfitting models to the locked corpus. Mitigation: rotate locked seed sets monthly and keep an independent stochastic spot-check job.
2026-03-12 Design feedback (internal): Ensure stability matrix cells include an example prompt anchor for human triage when a cell regresses (UX for triage).
